# protocol_golden_vectors_reliability.txt -- cross-language conformance
# fixture for the 2026-08-21 reliability-layer retarget (sprint 007
# ticket 012). Supersedes protocol_golden_vectors.txt for this
# harness's fixture-driven blocks -- that file gates the PRE-retarget
# (optional-id, `ok`-bearing) scheme and is marked superseded in place,
# kept but no longer read by this harness.
#
# Design authority: reference/protocol-draft-2026-08-21.md, this repo's
# own verbatim snapshot of radio-robot-lib's docs/design/protocol.md
# (uncommitted working tree, base commit c99e6e8) -- every vector below
# is a mechanical instance of that snapshot's own tables (Sec 6's verb
# table, Sec 8.1's three-way classification table, Sec 8.3's ESTOP
# forgiveness matrix, Sec 6.3's RUN outcome table) or a literal worked
# example it states directly, cited per block. Written from those
# tables FIRST, then confirmed against the implementation -- not
# authored after the fact to match whatever the code happened to emit.
#
# ---- format (same structural parser this harness already used for
# the pre-retarget fixture -- tests/unit/_protocol_fixture.py) ----
#
# Blocks are separated by one or more blank lines. Comment lines start
# with '#'. Each block is, in order:
#   zero or more SETUP lines   -- arm a FRESH mock adapter's canned
#                                  answers (this harness constructs a
#                                  brand new ProtocolHandler/Adapter/
#                                  Sink per block -- expected_next
#                                  always starts at 1)
#   one or more ACTION lines   -- IN <wire line> | EMIT <col spec...>
#                                  | DEBUG [<text>]
#   zero or more OUT lines     -- expected reply lines, in order,
#                                  accumulated across every ACTION in
#                                  the block (the sink is never cleared
#                                  mid-block -- this is what lets a
#                                  multi-action block prove a SEQUENCE
#                                  of ack/nack/err lines, e.g. gap ->
#                                  stall -> self-heal), OR the single
#                                  line "OUT NONE" meaning the sink
#                                  must be EMPTY after every ACTION in
#                                  the block runs.
#
# SETUP keys:
#   identity <name> <serial> <drivetrain> <profile> <version>
#   now <uint32>
#   status <ready> <active> <connL> <connR> <otos> <wedge> <flags> <tlm>
#     (ready/active/connL/connR/otos/wedge are 0 or 1; flags is decimal,
#     formatted as hex on the wire; tlm is the literal lowercase word)
#   getoverride <name> <value>
#   fieldnames <name1> [<name2> ...]   -- bare GET's enumeration order
#   setresult / wheelsresult / stopresult / runresult <ordinal>
#     -- Protocol::Result's declaration-order ordinal (0=OK, 1=UNKNOWN,
#        2=BADARG, 3=RANGE, 4=FULL, 5=UNIMPLEMENTED, 6=NOT_CONFIGURED,
#        7=BUSY, 8=DUPLICATE_ID) -- same table this harness's own
#        pre-retarget SETUP keys already used
#   runvalue <text>       -- the canned on_run() return value
#   runhasvalue <0 or 1>  -- whether on_run() reports a value at all
#                             (void vs. value-returning, Sec 6.3)
#
# EMIT column spec: one or more "<name>:<hex0or1>:<value>" tokens --
# this fixture's own SETUP/EMIT sub-syntax, unrelated to the wire
# grammar; never fed through feed(), only unpacked and passed to
# emit_telemetry().

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.1 / Sec 6: in-order ack, one block per verb family. The ack
# fires UNCONDITIONALLY before the verb's own reply (Sec 9.8 item 4).
# =============================================================================

SETUP now 38472
IN PING #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT pong 38472

SETUP identity testbot SN001 differential tovez 6.0.0
IN ID #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT id differential tovez 6.0.0

SETUP identity testbot SN001 differential tovez 6.0.0
IN VER #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT ver 6.0.0

# STATUS's reply is spec Sec 4's own literal worked example line,
# extended 2026-08-21 with next=<expected_next> (Sec 8.7). flags=216
# equals spec Sec 6.2's own telemetry example flags value (0xd8).
SETUP status 1 0 1 1 1 0 216 pose
IN STATUS #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT status ready=1 active=0 connL=1 connR=1 otos=1 wedge=0 flags=d8 tlm=pose next=2

# HELP is "generated by walking the verb table at runtime" (Sec 4) --
# 13 verbs as of this retarget, RUN appended last (Sec 6/9.7).
IN HELP #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT help HELLO PING ID VER STATUS HELP GET SET TLM WHEELS STOP ESTOP RUN

SETUP getoverride wheel_control.pid_kp 0.03
IN GET wheel_control.pid_kp #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT get wheel_control.pid_kp 0.030000

# GET's own bare form (no name, just the id) dumps one line per
# adapter-declared field, in the adapter's own enumeration order --
# entirely the adapter's business, the handler holds no table (Sec 7).
SETUP fieldnames wheel_control.pid_kp wheel_control.pid_ki
SETUP getoverride wheel_control.pid_kp 0.03
SETUP getoverride wheel_control.pid_ki 0.002
IN GET #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT get wheel_control.pid_kp 0.030000
OUT get wheel_control.pid_ki 0.002000

# GET with an unknown name still gets the ack (already sent by the
# time GET's own body runs) but no `get` line and no `err` either --
# silent, not counted malformed (Sec 6's own table note).
IN GET no.such.field #1
OUT ack 1 0

# SET: "ok" is gone -- the ack IS the acceptance (Sec 8.2). Nothing
# follows a successful SET.
SETUP setresult 0
IN SET wheel_control.pid_kp 0.03 #1
OUT ack 1 0

# SET rejected by the adapter: the ack still fires (the line arrived,
# in order), and err is a SECOND line layered on top (Sec 8.2), field
# order code-first (Sec 8.6).
SETUP setresult 1
IN SET no.such.field 0.03 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 1 #1

IN TLM POSE #1
OUT ack 1 0

SETUP wheelsresult 0
IN WHEELS 100 100 1000 #1
OUT ack 1 0

SETUP stopresult 0
IN STOP #1
OUT ack 1 0

SETUP runresult 0
SETUP runvalue 42
SETUP runhasvalue 1
IN RUN echo 42 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT ret 42 #1

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.1's three-way table, in one chained block per case -- a fresh
# handler per BLOCK, but every IN action within ONE block shares that
# same handler/adapter, so `expected_next` genuinely advances across
# the chained lines below.
# =============================================================================

# In order (== expected_next): dispatch, advance, ack <id> <lastDone>.
# Retransmit (< expected_next), right after: do NOT re-execute -- ack
# echoes the highest ALREADY-accepted id, not the resent one.
SETUP wheelsresult 0
IN WHEELS 100 100 1000 #1
IN WHEELS 100 100 1000 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT ack 1 0

# Gap (> expected_next): discard, do NOT execute, nack <expected_next>
# <lastDone> -- naming the id the robot actually needs, not the one
# just received.
SETUP stopresult 0
IN STOP #5
OUT nack 1 0

# =============================================================================
# Gap stalls the stream on purpose: every subsequent line, however
# well-formed, keeps nacking until the missing id arrives -- a fresh
# nack per inbound line (self-healing if a `nack` itself is lost).
# Filling the gap resumes normal in-order dispatch immediately.
# =============================================================================

SETUP now 1
SETUP stopresult 0
IN PING #2
IN STOP #2
IN PING #1
IN STOP #2
OUT nack 1 0
OUT nack 1 0
OUT ack 1 0
OUT pong 1
OUT ack 2 0

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.4 item 3: content-level rejection of an IN-ORDER line -- ack
# fires unconditionally, THEN the malformed-shape err layers on top.
# =============================================================================

# Unrecognized verb, in-order id: ack, then err 1 (ERR_UNKNOWN).
IN FROB 1 2 3 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 1 #1

# WHEELS with an unparseable field, in-order id: ack, then err 2
# (ERR_BADARG) -- the field decode failure never reaches on_wheels().
SETUP wheelsresult 0
IN WHEELS notanumber 100 1000 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 2 #1

# WHEELS accepted by the handler but rejected by the adapter (e.g.
# range): ack, then err <result_code> -- the SAME two-line layering,
# just the rejection now comes from the adapter's own Result instead
# of a handler-level decode failure.
SETUP wheelsresult 3
IN WHEELS 100 100 1000 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 3 #1

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.4 items 1-2: no trailing field at all, or a trailing field that
# is not a well-formed '#[0-9]+' -- malformed, NO REPLY (not even a
# bare ack/nack -- there is nothing to sequence-check).
# =============================================================================

IN STOP
OUT NONE

IN STOP notanid
OUT NONE

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.3: HELLO resets the sequence -- a fresh HELLO after some
# traffic sets expected_next back to 1, so the very next id must be #1
# again, not a continuation of whatever came before.
# =============================================================================

SETUP now 7
SETUP identity testbot SN001 differential tovez 6.0.0
IN PING #1
IN HELLO
IN PING #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT pong 7
OUT device NEZHA2 robot testbot SN001
OUT ack 1 0
OUT pong 7

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.3: ESTOP's forgiveness matrix -- ANY line whose verb token is
# exactly ESTOP executes the stop and replies the bare word `estop`,
# regardless of trailing junk or arity. Never sequenced, never nacked.
# =============================================================================

IN ESTOP
OUT estop

IN ESTOP 1 2 3
OUT estop

IN ESTOP #5
OUT estop

IN ESTOP #abc
OUT estop

# =============================================================================
# Sec 6.3: RUN's full outcome matrix.
# =============================================================================

# Unknown function: ack + err 1 (ERR_UNKNOWN).
SETUP runresult 1
IN RUN nosuchfunction 1 2 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 1 #1

# Wrong arity / an argument that will not convert (the adapter's own
# call, since the handler does no type conversion at all, Sec 6.3):
# ack + err 2 (ERR_BADARG).
SETUP runresult 2
IN RUN echo notanumber #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 2 #1

# Function returns nothing (void): nothing beyond the ack.
SETUP runresult 0
SETUP runhasvalue 0
IN RUN beep #1
OUT ack 1 0

# Function returns a value: `ret <value> #<id>`, IN ADDITION to the
# ack (Sec 6.1/6.3).
SETUP runresult 0
SETUP runvalue 42
SETUP runhasvalue 1
IN RUN echo 42 #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT ret 42 #1

# Bare RUN, no fields at all -- not even the id -- is malformed per
# Sec 8.4 item 1 (no trailing field): no reply of any kind.
IN RUN
OUT NONE

# "RUN #7" -- the id consumed the only field, no function name at all
# -- still classifies as an in-order id (ack fires), then RUN's own
# handler sees zero remaining fields: ack + err 2 (Sec 6.3's own
# explicit example).
IN RUN #1
OUT ack 1 0
OUT err 2 #1

# =============================================================================
# Sec 8.5: emit_telemetry() piggybacks the current reliability line on
# EVERY call, after thdr (if due) and t -- no timer, rides the existing
# telemetry cadence. flags=216 (0xd8) is spec Sec 6.2's own example.
# =============================================================================

EMIT seq:0:1 flags:1:216
OUT thdr seq flags
OUT t 1 d8
OUT ack 0 0

# A gap outstanding at emission time piggybacks a nack instead of an
# ack -- still no execution, still the same "next id I actually need."
SETUP stopresult 0
IN STOP #5
EMIT seq:0:2 flags:1:216
OUT nack 1 0
OUT thdr seq flags
OUT t 2 d8
OUT nack 1 0

# =============================================================================
# Sec 6.2: debug -- unsolicited, robot-to-host only, never reached
# through feed() at all (no inbound wire form exists to test here).
# Sanitization: '\n'/'\r' stripped; empty/omitted text collapses onto
# the bare `debug` line with no dangling separator space.
# =============================================================================

DEBUG hello world
OUT debug hello world

DEBUG
OUT debug
